audit.why: Neeko owns levels 1-2 and everything from 6 onward; Cassiopeia's only window is 3-5 while Tangle-Barbs is down. That matches 40% over 60 games - the second-worst row in this slice - and both layers already read Neeko, Neeko, Skill, Skill, Neeko, Neeko, Neeko.

audit.whatIsWrong: Tangle-Barbs is the named matchup-defining cooldown in four fields with no duration and no range, and Pop Blossom is called 'the kill' with no cooldown.
audit.why: Tangle-Barbs is 12/11.5/11/10.5/10s at 1000 range and Pop Blossom is 120/105/90s. The 1000 range matters: it out-reaches Noxious Blast's 850, so she can open from outside Cassiopeia's poke. The 12-second downtime is the only window Cassiopeia gets in this lane, which makes the number the whole plan.
audit.corrected: 12s and 1000 range added to breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, report[5].t, spikes[0].text, whys[0] and wants.foe[0].

audit.whatIsWrong: MOST SERIOUS: two fields state that Neeko's root cancels Petrifying Gaze - whys[4] says 'any root cancels your Petrifying Gaze entirely' and spikes[2].text says 'if her E root lands first, your Petrifying Gaze never connects'. A root immobilises; it does not silence. Cassiopeia can cast Petrifying Gaze while rooted, and being rooted while facing Neeko is exactly the position the ultimate wants.
audit.why: Riot's Tangle-Barbs text describes damage and a root, with no silence or ability-block component anywhere. Riot's Petrifying Gaze text has no movement requirement - it stuns enemies in front of her that are facing her. The existing lines therefore talk a player out of the single button that saves her, which is the most costly kind of wrong advice on the page. Pop Blossom's stun is a different matter and is the thing that genuinely takes her ultimate away.
audit.corrected: spikes[2].text and whys[4] now say the root does not stop the cast and name Pop Blossom's stun as the real threat; the distinction is repeated in breakdown.cooldowns and report[5].t.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four fields attribute Twin Fang to Neeko - 'her Q bloom and Twin Fang hit you', 'a free Blooming Burst and Twin Fang trade', 'sets up a free Q bloom and Twin Fang before I can answer'. Twin Fang is Cassiopeia's E. Also the ability is Tangle-Barbs, written as 'Tangle Barbs' without the hyphen.
audit.why: Neeko's damage after a root is Blooming Burst plus the Shapesplitter third-attack proc; she has no Twin Fang. Handing the enemy your own ability makes the whole threat model unreadable.
audit.corrected: Twin Fang removed from every Neeko-side description in whys[0], early, wants.foe[0] and spikes[1].text; hyphen restored in the edited fields.

audit.whatIsWrong: mid says W 'can ground her if she tries to disengage' at levels 4-5, and wants.you[1] blurs grounding across her clone-engage.
audit.why: Pop Blossom is the only movement ability in Neeko's kit - it carries the dash flag and leaps her into the air. Shapesplitter sends a clone, it does not move Neeko. So before 6 there is nothing for the grounding to disable, and from 6 the grounding is genuinely excellent: a Miasma cloud under Neeko stops Pop Blossom's leap outright. This is the one matchup in my slice where the grounding is a real, decisive tool, and the text buried it under a generic disengage claim.
audit.corrected: mid and wants.you[1] now tie the grounding specifically to Pop Blossom's leap; dontsFull[1].d says the same.

audit.whatIsWrong: CHAMP_FULL tldr is verbatim Lucian boilerplate - 'He pokes in bursts, you poke forever' - with male pronouns for Neeko and a treadmill claim that is the opposite of this lane's shape.
audit.why: Cassiopeia does not grind Neeko down; she survives one root window and loses to the next. Also worth knowing and not currently anywhere: Inherent Glamour breaks on receiving immobilising crowd control, so a landed Petrifying Gaze strips her disguise.
audit.corrected: tldr rewritten to the actual matchup. The Inherent Glamour point is recorded here only - I had no band-safe field left to carry it.

edits.before: Neeko owns the early lane because her E (Tangle Barbs) root sets up a free Q bloom and Twin Fang before I can answer, and I have no mobility or shield to dodge it once it's flying. Level 1 I concede — one ability, no poison stacking yet, and her Blooming Burst chunks me if I step up to last-hit. My one window is level 2-3: if I sidestep her E and hold W (Miasma) to slow her, I can Q-prime and chain Twin Fang while her root is down. But if that root lands first I eat the full combo and lose the trade. Dodging E is the whole early game for me.
edits.after: Neeko owns the early lane because her Tangle-Barbs root reaches 1000 — further than my 850 Q — and sets up a free Blooming Burst before I can answer, with no mobility or shield to dodge it once it's flying. Level 1 I concede: one ability, no poison stacking, and Blooming Burst chunks me if I step up to last-hit. My one window is level 2-3: sidestep the root and it is gone for 12 seconds, and in that gap I Q-prime and chain Twin Fang freely. But if the root lands first I eat the full combo and lose the trade. Dodging Tangle-Barbs is the whole early game for me.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 I can claw it back toward even if I land Q poison and force extended trades — my ramping Twin Fang out-DPSes her squishy frame once I'm chaining it, and W can ground her if she tries to disengage. But 6 flips it hard to her: Pop Blossom out of fog or a disguised W clone lets her root-and-burst me, and a landed E means my Petrifying Gaze never goes off. With no defensive steroid besides move speed, one caught root at level 6 is lethal.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 I can claw it back toward even if I land Q poison and force extended trades — my ramping Twin Fang out-DPSes her squishy frame, and before 6 she has no dash to escape it. But 6 flips it hard to her: Pop Blossom out of fog or a disguised clone lets her root-and-burst me. The saving grace is that a root does not silence — I can still turn and fire Petrifying Gaze while held — and Miasma grounds the Pop Blossom leap.

edits.before: He pokes in bursts, you poke forever — survive the early chip and the treadmill out-grinds him.
edits.after: One root and you die — dodge Tangle-Barbs, ground her leap, and the poison does the rest.

notes: The costliest error in my whole slice is here: two fields told the player that Neeko's root cancels Petrifying Gaze. Roots immobilise, they do not silence, and being rooted while facing Neeko is precisely the position the ultimate is designed for — so the page was talking her out of the button that saves the fight. Second, Twin Fang was attributed to Neeko in four separate fields. Third, this is the one matchup in my slice where Miasma's grounding genuinely decides something (Pop Blossom is the only movement ability in her kit) and the text had it as a vague disengage line instead. Recorded but not written for want of a band-safe field: Inherent Glamour breaks on immobilising crowd control, so a landed Petrifying Gaze strips her disguise.
